summary: September 13, 2026 scope review of retained evidence, not a new execution campaign. Explicit current hardening obligations prevent historical Linux, macOS, Rust-only or baseline database success from qualifying a different platform, language or data revision. Empty claim lists are deliberate open obligations, not evidence that the feature does not exist.

qualification_requirements.acceptance: Preserve existing business rows through verified candidate activation; replay explicit checkpoint IDs after the installed runtime restarts. Does not qualify PostgreSQL or hard power loss.
Native save, conflict rejection, WebView restart, version reload and real solve retain identity without duplicate checkpoints. The caller retains the explicit key.

Execute revision-1 copy upgrade and revision-2 receipt concurrency, transaction rollback and restart replay on isolated PostgreSQL. The five skipped local PostgreSQL tests and the older baseline run do not satisfy this scope.

Restore one consistent generation of the database, external result files, Kcore artifacts and workflow recovery envelopes, verify lineage and run a healthy follow-up. A database-only snapshot is insufficient.

Installer blocks incompatible activation before opening active data for writes, exposes a digest-bound candidate and retains a usable rollback on failed activation. Package-only replacement does not qualify database cutover.
GUI exposes data inventory, retained bytes, plan, approval, progress, verification and safe recovery. Manual maintenance eval and file switching are not this user journey.

Expose a bounded durable recovery receipt for an uncertain GUI save after WebView closure, reconcile its outcome without silent re-save and offer an explicit next step. Current in-memory retry and an externally retained PWDT key are partial building blocks only.

Retain actual installed fault-injection evidence for service loss or response loss with recovery and no duplicated writes. Mock HTTP failures and a clean native restart do not close installed-macos fault recovery.

Close fault_injection_and_recovery/installed-windows using actual installed service or response loss, reconcile writes without duplication and complete a healthy follow-up. A clean startup or another platform's recovery does not satisfy this scope.
Close packaged_desktop_round_trip/windows-installed for Hub with native observable actions, backend effects and a reversible handoff. Linux/macOS shell evidence cannot substitute.
Close packaged_desktop_round_trip/windows-installed for Workbench with a saved study, native rendering, real run and reload. A Windows Operator SDK run is a different surface.
Close packaged_desktop_round_trip/windows-installed for Installer with actual setup, managed lifecycle and inspectable failure recovery, not compilation alone.
Close upgrade_and_rollback/packaged-desktop-set-windows with verified bundle-set replacement and a healthy rollback. Agent package installation is not desktop-set replacement.
Close remote_agent_orchestra_round_trip/installed-windows with the installed control path and healthy next-task execution; retain host and runtime identity.
Retain source-detached installed Rust SDK research and post-failure recovery with real solver evidence. This is retained historical evidence, not a fresh run on the current revision.
Retain the installed Python package's source-detached study/save/run/export/recovery journey on managed services. Cross-language mock parity and installed Rust execution cannot promote this scope.
Retain the installed Elixir SDK package's source-detached study/save/run/export/recovery journey on managed services. Rust-only installed evidence does not close it.
Preserve the existing scoped cross-language parity qualification without reinterpreting it as installed native execution.
Preserve retained macOS installed startup evidence; do not broadcast it to Windows or every Hub workflow.
Preserve retained Linux installed startup evidence; data migration and Windows bundle-set update remain separate obligations.
